title: Cost attribution: add experiment_id + variant to metering dimensions
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Internal: Cost attribution now supports experiment/variant breakdown for route-level A/B testing dashboards (token + GPU cost).
body: Summary: This PR attaches route-level A/B experiment dimensions (experiment_id and variant) to the cost attribution pipeline so Console reporting can compare unit economics across variants (token cost, GPU time cost) without requiring any customer-defined metrics. Context: Route-level A/B testing needs per-variant cost deltas, aligned with the same assignment used by the gateway exposure events; today metering/cost events are aggregated by (org, project, route, model, region, etc.) and we lose the variant dimension. What changed: (1) Metering event model now optionally includes experiment_id and experiment_variant (string) and propagates those tags through the cost attribution service; (2) The token accounting path (prompt_tokens/completion_tokens/total_tokens) and GPU attribution path (gpu_ms, accelerator_type) both carry the same experiment tags; (3) Aggregation tables/materialized views now group by experiment_id + experiment_variant when present, while preserving existing groupings when absent; (4) Added guardrails to avoid cardinality blowups: allowlisted dimension keys, max length checks, and a drop-on-violation counter; (5) Feature gating: tagging is enabled only when the request context indicates an active experiment assignment and the global ab_testing_cost_dimensions flag is on (defaults off outside staging/dogfood). Schema notes: New fields are optional; if absent, cost events behave exactly as before. Names are aligned with exposure logging work (see ADR-0188) but we intentionally keep the cost tag as experiment_variant (not variant_id) because variants are customer-visible strings in Console and are stable across reruns. Example (illustrative): cost_event.tags now may include {"experiment_id":"exp_01HP...","experiment_variant":"control"}. Changed areas/files (high level): services/metering/cost_event.go (add optional tags + validation); services/metering/attribution/attributor.go (propagate dims into cost buckets); services/telemetry/ingest/validators (allowlist + maxlen); analytics/warehouse/views/cost_by_route.sql (grouping + backfill-safe COALESCE); console-api/contracts/costQuery.proto (add optional filter dims); tests: metering attribution unit tests, golden aggregation test, validator tests. Rollout/ops: No backfill required; historical data remains untagged. Dashboards that query per-variant cost should expect missing data prior to tag rollout. Metrics: added meter.cost_tags_dropped_total{reason=} and meter.cost_events_tagged_total to track adoption and guardrail triggers. Verification: ran staging dogfood with an active experiment (50/50) and confirmed cost_by_variant sums match cost_by_route within ~0.2% (sampling/async windows) and variant splits approximately align with exposure counts. Checklist: [x] Backwards compatible schema; [x] Cardinality guardrails; [x] Unit + integration tests; [x] Added basic docs comment in code; [x] Linked to ENG-2842/2844. Review discussion highlights: Logan Wright: asked to confirm naming consistency with exposure logs and to ensure we can join on experiment_id + variant in the warehouse; I renamed tag key from variant to experiment_variant to reduce collisions with other systems and added a comment in the warehouse view explaining join semantics. Allison Grant: requested explicit cardinality limits and a drop counter; added max length (64) and allowlist enforcement plus dropped_total metric. Caleb Johnson: flagged that adding dimensions to cost events could unintentionally increase series count in Prometheus-style exporters; clarified that this is warehouse aggregation and the only new time-series is the dropped/tagged counters (low-cardinality), not per-experiment metrics. Jada Williams: asked about precedence when assignment is missing/unknown; I set behavior to omit tags entirely when assignment is not present or is "unknown" to avoid mixing costs into an "unknown" bucket that would confuse Console users. CI: Initial run failed gofmt + a flaky warehouse golden test (window alignment); reran after fixing deterministic ordering in the test harness. Final checks: build (pass), unit tests (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass).
commits: metering: extend CostEvent tags with experiment_id + experiment_variant
attribution: propagate experiment dimensions through token + GPU cost paths
warehouse: update cost aggregation views to group by experiment dims when present
validators: add allowlist + maxlen checks for experiment tags; emit dropped counter
console-api: extend cost query contract with optional experiment filters
tests: attribution tagging + warehouse aggregation golden coverage
conversation: Logan Wright (review): Can we align key names with exposure events? Exposure uses variant_label in some drafts; also please confirm warehouse join plan.

Nadia Rahman (author): Updated to experiment_variant (string label) + experiment_id; added a note in the SQL view about joining on (experiment_id, experiment_variant) with exposure aggregates. Exposure PR will emit the same variant label.
Allison Grant (review): Please add explicit max length + allowlist on these new tags; we’ve been burned by high-cardinality tag creep.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added allowlist enforcement, maxlen=64, and meter.cost_tags_dropped_total{reason=} for visibility. Also added meter.cost_events_tagged_total to track rollout.
Caleb Johnson (review): Are we exporting these tags to any metrics backend where it explodes series count? Want to avoid per-experiment time series by default.
Nadia Rahman (author): No per-experiment metrics emitted here. These are tags on cost events going to attribution + warehouse. Only new counters are dropped/tagged totals (bounded labels).
Jada Williams (review): What happens when assignment is unavailable (e.g., retries, missing hash key)? Please avoid an "unknown" bucket in UI.
Nadia Rahman (author): Agreed; when assignment is missing/unknown we omit experiment tags entirely. That keeps costs in the baseline route/model buckets and avoids misleading UI buckets.
Vikram Singh (review): Any concerns with Dedicated vs Hosted metering paths? We have some slight differences in how GPU attribution is attached.

Nadia Rahman (author): Verified both paths: the tags are attached at the request context layer before branching; added a regression test covering the GPU attribution path with experiment tags present.
Logan Wright (approval): Looks good after rename + SQL note. Approved.
Allison Grant (approval): Guardrails look solid. Approved.
Caleb Johnson (approval): Thanks for clarifying metrics impact. Approved.
Jada Williams (approval): Behavior on missing assignment is what we want. Approved.
